purpose: Messy real-world tabular files for taxonomy validation (stream A). Raw files are gitignored; this manifest + fetch_corpus.py reproduce them. Every entry notes source and license.

entries.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use

entries.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (ONS)
entries.note: ONS CDID JP9Z time series via the generator?format=csv endpoint. Classic ONS shape: 8 metadata/preamble rows (Title, CDID, Source dataset ID, PreUnit, Unit, Release date, Next release, Important notes) above the real header, then mixed-frequency observations in one column — annual rows like "2002", quarterly like "2001 Q2", and monthly like "2016 APR" all interleaved.

entries.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (ONS)
entries.note: ONS CDID HQTI (Services Producer Price Index). Same preamble-metadata-rows-above-header pattern as the other ONS files; smaller series, good minimal-size example of the format for parser unit tests.

entries.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (ONS)
entries.note: ONS CDID IHYQ (GDP quarter-on-quarter growth, CVM SA %). Same preamble/mixed-frequency shape; values include negative percentages, useful alongside the other two ONS files for testing a parser against several distinct series without re-deriving the format.

entries.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (Department for Transport, gov.uk statistical data set)
entries.note: DfT VEH0160 licensed vehicles by make/model/fuel, UK. Wide/pivoted shape: one row per Make+GenModel+Model+Fuel combination with ~50 quarter columns ("2026 Q1" ... "2005 Q1") as the header, i.e. requires unpivot to long/tidy form; blank cells where a model wasn't on the register that quarter. Medium-large file (~10MB), good candidate for the 1-20MB tier.

entries.license: Open Government Licence (Leicester City Council open data portal, listed via data.gov.uk catalogue)
entries.encoding_observed: UTF-8 with BOM (double/duplicated BOM bytes observed at file start: \xef\xbb\xbf\xef\xbb\xbf)
entries.note: Licensed hackney carriage/private hire vehicles for Leicester. Semicolon-delimited despite being UK/English-language (Opendatasoft-style export default), ISO-style YYYY-MM-DD dates, and an unusual doubled UTF-8 BOM at the very start of the file — a good encoding-detection edge case.

entries.license: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence (Etalab), per Toulouse Métropole open data portal terms
entries.note: 2019 EU election candidate lists, Toulouse. Semicolon-delimited, French accented uppercase text (É, ÉCOLOGIE, RÉVOLTE) mixed with civility abbreviations (M., Mme). Tiny file, useful as a minimal French-locale fixture.

entries.license: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence (Etalab), Toulouse Métropole
entries.note: Pedestrian counts 2006-2019. Semicolon-delimited; geo_point_2d as a "lat, lon" string AND a geo_shape column containing an embedded double-quoted JSON blob (GeoJSON Point) inside the CSV cell — nested-structure-in-a-cell edge case.

entries.license: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence (Etalab), Toulouse Métropole
entries.note: Weather station archive, La Salade, 2021. Semicolon delimiter, French column names, ISO timestamps; a per-station-type sensor table where some fields are naturally sparse depending on sous_station.

entries.license: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence (Etalab), Toulouse Métropole
entries.note: Municipal budget line items, Blagnac 2022. Semicolon-delimited French public-finance nomenclature (chapitre/article codes), two parallel monetary columns (mt_vote_bp_depense / mt_vote_bp_recette) where exactly one is populated per row and the other is blank.

entries.license: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence (Etalab), Toulouse Métropole
entries.note: 2013 INSEE census by grand quartier, activity breakdown. Semicolon-delimited, very wide (dozens of p13_* numeric columns), embedded geo_shape polygon JSON per row, INSEE codes as zero-padded strings that a naive parser will coerce to numbers and lose leading zeros on.

entries.license: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence (Etalab), Nantes Métropole open data portal

School canteen menus across Nantes Métropole communes. Semicolon-delimited, UTF-8 BOM, one plain-text repas column and a parallel repas_html column containing the same content wrapped in raw
HTML — HTML-in-CSV-cell edge case; accented French food terms throughout.

entries.license: Datenlizenz Deutschland / Stadt Konstanz open data portal terms (offenedaten-konstanz.de)
entries.note: Hourly bicycle counter data, Konstanz bridge (Herose), 2018. Semicolon-delimited, German DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM timestamps, three parallel directional count columns.

entries.note: Bicycle counter site metadata, Würzburg. English column headers on a German dataset (portal default export labels), semicolon-delimited, lat/lon packed into one "Coordinates" string column, sparse Installation Date/photourl fields. Tiny fixture-sized file.

entries.license: Munich Open Data Portal (opendata.muenchen.de), typically CC-BY 4.0 — confirm exact licence on dataset page before redistribution
entries.encoding_observed: UTF-8 with BOM, comma-delimited (unlike the other DE files, which are semicolon)
entries.note: Munich population by year since 1900. Comma-delimited (portal-inconsistent with the semicolon convention seen elsewhere in DE), UTF-8 BOM, early rows (1900) have blank einwohner_deutsche/einwohner_auslaender_innen because that breakdown wasn't collected yet — genuine historical-schema-drift nulls, not random missingness.

entries.license: Japan Meteorological Agency data usage terms
entries.note: Companion 24-hour precipitation totals file, same JMA endpoint family and Shift_JIS encoding as the 1h file; kept both since the two exercise slightly different column layouts under the same encoding condition.

entries.license: US Census Bureau public domain (US government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

entries.license: NOAA NCEI public domain (US government work)
entries.note: SLICED: source file decompresses to 75,593 rows / ~72.9MB, well over the ~30MB cap; truncated to the header plus the first 30,000 data rows (~40% of rows) to land at ~29.2MB, just under the cap — noting the slice here per instructions. Storm Events Database, 2023. DAMAGE_PROPERTY/DAMAGE_CROPS use suffix-scaled string sentinels like "10.00K"/"2.5M" instead of plain numbers, TOR_* tornado-only columns are blank for all non-tornado EVENT_TYPE rows (conditional sparsity by category), long free-text EPISODE_NARRATIVE/EVENT_NARRATIVE fields contain embedded commas and quotes requiring correct CSV quoting.
